authority: Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs; operated through Post Offices and authorised banks (SBI, Bank of Baroda, etc.)

description.en: The Public Provident Fund (PPF) is a long-term savings scheme backed by the Government of India offering tax-free returns. It has a 15-year lock-in period (extendable in 5-year blocks) with partial withdrawal allowed from the 7th year. Deposits qualify for tax deduction under Section 80C, and both interest earned and maturity proceeds are tax-free (EEE status).

verifiedConditions.claim: Only resident Indians can open a PPF account. NRIs are not eligible to open a new PPF account, though existing accounts opened before becoming NRI can be maintained until maturity.
An individual can hold only one PPF account. A second account opened in violation is treated as irregular and earns no interest.

unverifiedEligibility: A minor can have a PPF account opened on their behalf by a guardian, but only one account per minor.
Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) are not eligible to open PPF accounts (since 2005).
Joint accounts are not permitted under the PPF scheme.

requirements.claim: PPF Account opening form (Form A for post office, or bank-specific form) duly filled and signed.
Valid identity proof — Aadhaar card, PAN card, voter ID, passport, or driving license.
Proof of address — Aadhaar, utility bill, bank statement, or passport.
Two recent passport-size photographs of the account holder.
PAN card or Form 60 (if PAN not available) is required for KYC compliance.
Initial deposit of minimum Rs. 500 (and maximum Rs. 1,50,000 per financial year) via cash, cheque, demand draft, or online transfer.
Nomination form (Form E) to designate a nominee for the PPF account. Recommended but not mandatory for account opening.

processInformation.claim: Choose between a post office or an authorised bank (SBI, Bank of Baroda, Bank of India, Central Bank of India, Punjab National Bank, etc.) to open the PPF account. Online account opening is available at most major banks through net banking.
Submit the filled application form along with KYC documents and the initial deposit. For online applications, upload scanned copies of documents and make the deposit through net banking or UPI.

After document verification, the PPF account is activated and a passbook is issued. The account number is generated immediately for online applications. Subsequent deposits can be made in a lump sum or in up to 12 instalments during the financial year.

output.claim: A PPF passbook is issued containing the account number, holder details, and deposit records. The account has a 15-year tenure with an option to extend in blocks of 5 years. Interest is credited annually at the rate declared by the Ministry of Finance (currently 7.1% p.a., compounded annually). The account qualifies for EEE (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) tax status.

fees.claim: No account opening fee or maintenance charges. The only requirement is the minimum annual deposit of Rs. 500.

fees.applicability: Annual deposit range per financial year
fees.claim: Minimum annual deposit is Rs. 500 and maximum is Rs. 1,50,000 per financial year. Deposits can be made in a lump sum or up to 12 instalments. Failure to deposit the minimum amount incurs a penalty of Rs. 50 per year of default plus the minimum subscription.

processingTime.applicability: PPF account opening at bank branch or post office
processingTime.claim: PPF account is typically opened on the same day when applying at a bank branch or post office with complete documents. Online account opening through net banking is instant. Post office applications may take 1-2 days if document verification is pending.

claimsSupported: Account can be opened at any post office.
Deposits in up to 12 instalments per financial year.
Partial withdrawal allowed from 7th financial year.
Loan facility available from 3rd to 6th financial year.
Premature closure allowed after 5 years under specific conditions.
sources.uncertainty: Specific operational procedures may vary between post offices and banks.

limitations: Interest rate is subject to quarterly revision by the Ministry of Finance and may change.
This record does not cover PPF loan facility, partial withdrawal, or premature closure procedures in detail.
Transfer of PPF account between bank and post office is available but the process is not detailed here.
NRI rules regarding continuation of existing accounts may vary based on RBI guidelines.
Online account opening procedures vary between banks.
